solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: State how one works with leather in North America

parts.note: MO is modus operandi, the way someone habitually works

indicators.note: in places the leather inside the North America abbreviation

parts.note: tan is tanned leather or the act of tanning hides

explanation.surface: A clue asking how a leatherworker practises their trade on the American continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a verb meaning say, but it is the definition; MO is modus operandi, a person's way of working.
explanation.definitionFit: Montana is one of the fifty United States, so it is an example of a state.

clue.text: Fat cat finding small insect amid Mother Earth

indicators.note: amid means the insect sits in the middle of the mother and earth letters

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
a gnat is a small biting fly

explanation.surface: Someone discovers a tiny insect buried in the soil of Mother Earth.
explanation.definitionFit: A fat cat is slang for a wealthy, powerful businessperson, which is what a tycoon or magnate is.

clue.text: Disreputable number contracted to foreign port, American

parts.note: No. is the shortened form of the word number
Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port, often shortened to Rio
US stands for American, as in US forces

explanation.surface: A disreputable figure has been signed to a foreign port by an American.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone notorious is famous for bad reasons, so they are disreputable.

clue.text: Abundant booze attracts party man

indicators.note: attracts means the booze draws the politician into itself

parts.note: ale is beer, a kind of booze
an MP is a Member of Parliament, typically a party politician

explanation.surface: Free drink pulls in a party politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party man' is a politician, a Member of Parliament, not a reveller; 'attracts' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Ample supplies are plentiful, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: High-flyer from Scotland primarily traverses region there

parts.note: Alba is the Gaelic name for Scotland

indicators.note: primarily means only the first letter of traverses is wanted

parts.note: Ross is a region of the Scottish Highlands, as in Ross and Cromarty

explanation.surface: A high-flyer from Scotland crosses a Scottish region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'there' points back to Scotland, so the region is a Scottish one: Ross, in the Highlands.
explanation.definitionFit: The albatross is a great seabird known for long soaring flights, so it is literally a high flyer.

clue.text: Aromatic flavouring one needs to sprinkle on bit of aubergine

indicators.note: bit of means just the opening letter of aubergine
to sprinkle means the letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A cooking tip: a spice should be scattered over a piece of aubergine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to sprinkle' rearranges I and NEEDS into NISEED, which goes 'on' the A from aubergine.
explanation.definitionFit: The seed of the anise plant tastes of liquorice and is used as an aromatic flavouring.

clue.text: Totter perhaps, having seen venomous creature

definitions.meaning: a totter is one who tots up figures, i.e. adds them
the snake also called a viper, Britain's only venomous one

explanation.surface: Someone tottering about has just spotted a poisonous snake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Totter' looks like a person unsteady on their feet, but it means one who tots up sums.
explanation.definitionFit: One who tots up a column of numbers adds them; the viper of that name is a venomous snake.

clue.text: British novelist's home contains excellent raised borders

indicators.note: contains means the home word holds the excellent one inside

parts.note: being in means being at home
A1 means first-rate, written here as AI
banks are raised edges, as of a river or flowerbed

explanation.surface: A writer's house has fine raised flowerbeds.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 (top quality) is written with the letter I for the figure 1.
explanation.definitionFit: Iain Banks was a Scottish author of The Wasp Factory and the Culture science-fiction series.

clue.text: Praise partner once lifting patch of ground

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: lifting in a down clue means the word is turned upwards, read backwards

parts.note: a lot is a plot of land

explanation.surface: Someone praises a former partner for picking up a bit of land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifting' turns LOT upwards in this down entry, giving TOL.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol someone is to praise them highly, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Maybe Nureyev nursed a wound

indicators.note: wound, from winding, means the letters are twisted round into a new order

explanation.surface: Perhaps the famous dancer tended an injury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wound' looks like an injury but is the past tense of wind, rearranging NURSED A.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudolf Nureyev was a celebrated male ballet dancer, an example of a danseur.

clue.text: Ascended pass with sheep

parts.note: to go can mean to pass, as time goes or passes
a tup is a ram, a male sheep

explanation.surface: Someone climbed a mountain pass along with a sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting up means rising or climbing, so it can mean ascended.

clue.text: Poor-quality porcelain in which rackets are involved

parts.note: bad means of poor quality
Minton is a famous Staffordshire make of fine china

explanation.surface: Cheap china that turns out to be part of a criminal racket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rackets' suggests criminal schemes; here they are the bats used to hit a shuttlecock.
explanation.definitionFit: The sport is played with rackets and a shuttlecock, so rackets are involved in it.

clue.text: Circulate landlord's correspondence

parts.note: to air an idea is to circulate it
a letter is one who lets property, a landlord

explanation.surface: A landlord's letters are being passed around.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerogramme, a lightweight sheet folded into its own envelope, is an item of correspondence sent by airmail.

clue.text: Part of leg lubricated when reviewing swelling

indicators.note: reviewing, read as re-viewing, means looking at those letters backwards
part of means the letters lie inside the phrase leg lubricated

explanation.surface: Someone checks on a swollen leg after rubbing oil into it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part of' takes EGLUB from leG LUBricated and 'reviewing' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A bulge is a rounded swelling or protuberance, so the nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Recording studio's last award for a long time

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: last means only the final letter of studio is wanted

parts.note: CH is the Companion of Honour, a British honour

explanation.surface: A recording studio wins its final prize in ages.
explanation.walkthrough: CH is the Companion of Honour, an order awarded by the British monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: An epoch is an era or a long period of history.

clue.text: Teacher Mark, the latest on Bake- Off making adornment for loaf

parts.note: the head is the head teacher of a school
a scar is a mark left on the skin

indicators.note: the latest means the very last letter of the show's name

explanation.surface: A teacher called Mark creates a decoration for a loaf on The Great British Bake Off.
explanation.walkthrough: Loaf is slang for head (from rhyming slang loaf of bread). Bake Off is a British television baking contest.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloth worn over the hair adorns the head, and loaf is a slang word for head.

clue.text: Cross-country athlete, regularly logging four miles, never keeps time

indicators.note: regularly logging means recording every other letter of four miles
keeps means the never word holds the time letter inside

parts.note: ne'er is the poetic shortening of never

explanation.surface: A runner records four miles at regular intervals but never times them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly logging' takes the 2nd, 4th, 6th and 8th letters of fOuR mIlEs; 'keeps' puts T inside NE'ER.
explanation.definitionFit: An orienteer competes in a sport of navigating across open country with map and compass.

clue.text: Whatever happens, it's foolish to recruit unknown accountants

indicators.note: to recruit means the foolish word takes the others in

parts.note: inane means silly or foolish
Y is a mathematical unknown, like x
CAs are chartered accountants

explanation.surface: Whatever happens, hiring an unknown team of accountants is silly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to recruit' signals the insertion; in algebra x and y are the usual unknowns.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means regardless or no matter what, an idiom for whatever happens.

clue.text: Piece of meat one rests here during main course?

indicators.note: during means the bed word comes in the middle of the main course

parts.note: an entree is the main course of a meal in American use
a cot is a small bed where one rests

explanation.surface: A diner pauses for a rest in the middle of the main course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' signals the insertion; the question mark admits that a bed in the middle of dinner is fanciful.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrecote is a boned steak cut from between the ribs, a piece of meat.

clue.text: The main beverage attracting staff aboard carrier

indicators.note: attracting means the beverage pulls the rest into itself

parts.note: tea is a common beverage

indicators.note: aboard means the staff word goes on to the carrier, inside it

parts.note: an ass is a beast of burden that carries loads
to man a post is to staff it

explanation.surface: A drink served to the crew on board a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' looks like the main point but is poetic for the sea; 'aboard' and 'attracting' each signal an insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: The main is a poetic word for the open sea, and this is the sea between Australia and New Zealand.

clue.text: Contemporary star on extreme type of diet?

indicators.note: on in a down clue means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: top is used for star, as in top of the bill
1 CAL, written ICAL, is one calorie, an extreme diet indeed

explanation.surface: A celebrity is on a fashionable extreme diet.
explanation.walkthrough: The figure 1 is written as I, so 1 CAL becomes ICAL; the question mark flags this playful reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Topical matters relate to current events, so topical means contemporary.

clue.text: Protest is about money

indicators.note: about means the word is turned round backwards

parts.note: tin is old slang for money

explanation.surface: A protest that is really about money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning' but signals the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: A sit-in is a form of protest in which people occupy a place and refuse to leave.

clue.text: You're welcome, son, to enter immediately and have some food

indicators.note: to enter means the son letter goes into the immediately word

parts.note: now means immediately
to eat is to have some food

explanation.surface: A host welcomes a son, urging him to come in at once and eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to enter' puts S inside NOW.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an informal reply to thanks, meaning it was no trouble at all.

clue.text: Turned up with member's footwear

indicators.note: turned means the following word is read backwards

parts.note: MP's: a Member of Parliament's

explanation.surface: An MP arrives in smart shoes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned' makes UP into PU.
explanation.definitionFit: Pumps are light shoes such as plimsolls or court shoes, so they are footwear.

clue.text: He led an exodus from Spain through boggy ground

indicators.note: through means Spain's letter runs within the boggy ground word

parts.note: a moss is a peat bog in northern English and Scots use
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A leader takes refugees out of Spain across marshland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'through' puts E inside MOSS; 'from' is a link word, though it reads like part of the exodus.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible, Moses led the Israelites out of Egypt in the Exodus.

clue.text: Cowboy "awfully sorry" about old car number that's bent over

indicators.note: about means the anagrammed word surrounds the other pieces
awfully means the letters of sorry are badly mangled
bent over means the number is folded back to front

parts.note: a reg is a British vehicle registration number

explanation.surface: A cowboy apologises profusely for bending an old number plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' makes ROYRS; 'bent over' signals the reversal and 'about' the insertion. A reg is a British number plate.
explanation.definitionFit: Roy Rogers was a famous singing cowboy star of American films and television.

clue.text: Haggard jockey?

definitions.meaning: the middle name of H. ... Haggard, the author of King Solomon's Mines
a jockey is one who rides racehorses

explanation.surface: A jockey looking worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Haggard' is not exhausted: it is the novelist H. Rider Haggard.
explanation.definitionFit: The novelist was named Henry Rider Haggard, and a jockey is someone on horseback in a race.

clue.text: Somebody grabs copper at the perfect moment

indicators.note: grabs means somebody's word seizes the copper symbol inside

parts.note: one means somebody, as in one should
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: Someone seizes a police officer just in time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a police officer; it is the metal, symbol Cu.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase comes from theatre, where an actor comes in exactly on a prompt, at just the right time.

clue.text: Greek who predicted when hospital doctor would settle in California

indicators.note: would settle in means the other pieces take up residence inside California

parts.note: CA is the postal abbreviation for California
as means when, as in as I left
san is short for sanatorium

explanation.surface: A Greek prophet foretold when a hospital doctor would move to California.
explanation.walkthrough: 'would settle in' signals the insertion; 'san' is short for sanatorium.
explanation.definitionFit: Cassandra, a Trojan princess in Greek myth, was given the gift of prophecy but cursed never to be believed.

clue.text: Cold duck needing spice

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
a duck is a score of zero in cricket, and love is zero in tennis

explanation.surface: A cold duck dish crying out for seasoning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck' is not the bird: in cricket it is a score of nothing, which in tennis is love.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloves are dried flower buds used as a kitchen spice.

clue.text: Eagerly desire Lotus when travelling around France with Rex

indicators.note: around means the anagrammed letters go round the France letter
when travelling means the letters of Lotus are moved about

parts.note: F is the international vehicle code for France
R stands for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A man longs for a Lotus sports car to tour France with his friend Rex.
explanation.walkthrough: Lotus is a British sports car maker. 'when travelling' turns LOTUS into LUSTO, and 'around' puts it round F.
explanation.definitionFit: To lust for something is to crave it intensely, i.e. to desire it eagerly.

clue.text: Head away from most dangerous mountain

indicators.note: head away from means the opening letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: severest means harshest or most dangerous

explanation.surface: Someone turns back from the deadliest peak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head away from' removes the S at the front of SEVEREST.
explanation.definitionFit: Everest, on the Nepal-Tibet border, is the world's highest mountain.
